mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates cheap borrowing costs, stimulating investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher during low FEDFUNDS periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment rate signals economic strength, boosting consumer and business confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow significant UNRATE decreases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and low federal funds rate jointly indicate strong demand and easy monetary conditions, boosting equity markets.
regime_hint: economic expansion with low interest rates
failure_condition: No positive correlation between GDPC1 growth and low FEDFUNDS on SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts signal strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns, especially in economic expansion regimes.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow housing starts growth in expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate increases borrowing costs, reducing investment and consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not follow high FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow INDPRO growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment and high federal funds rate indicate tight labor market and high rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns due to potential inflation and rate hikes.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not follow low UNRATE and high FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rate in late-cycle expansion signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative returns do not follow UNRATE increases in late-cycle (t-test p > 0.05).
